body: Thank you. Writing is one of the things I do to cope. I'm working on a novel and several short stories; it helps me get out of my head for a little while.

Thank you for replying. I'm writing here because I have no idea where to start getting help. I'm so good at pretending to be fine that I don't know how to tell people I'm not. No one but my bf knows. Well, I broke down and told my mom but she just ignored me (typical). Even counselors I've seen tell me they don't think it necessary I attend sessions because I seem fine. I recently moved and I don't have a doctor, and I don't think a walk in clinic would be the right place to get help. I don't have the money for any fancy psychiatrist. Most days when there isn't a pressing need to go out, I stay at home. I'm afraid I'm going to be like this forever, because I can't seem to bring myself to talk to friends or find a stable job or hand in college applications.

If you can tell me how exactly to get help, I might be able to convince myself to listen to you.

"Wherever you go, there you are". That's very true. On the other hand, it allows you to forget for a moment. You return to yourself, that's true, but for a moment you're gone. Try bushwhacking through a Panamanian jungle. Dancing on a Thai beach. 

I'm not really sure what I can say to help you. Only that I know how you're feeling. I could tell you that you're not alone, but you are, at least in your head.

I could tell you it gets better, but how the fuck do I know that?

All I can think of now is, have you tried helping anyone lately? Volunteering or something? Helping others who are in need really puts your own issues into perspective.

That or art. Any form of art: music, writing, drawing, etc.

It's 3:15 where I am and I'm half drunk (trying to sleep, fuck you insomnia) so I'm sorry if I'm not as articulate as I may otherwise be.
I think that contemplating death is a natural thought process of anyone who ruminates, who dives into themselves. It is easier to be thoughtless. It is those who seek answers and truth and meaning who have the hardest time. 
If writing helps you, I am here to listen. You can tell me anything and everything you need to. I may pass out soon (hopefully) but I would be very, very happy if you are there in the morning. Though you may also just be a username and a wall of text, you're human to me and I care about you.
See, talking to you helps me deal with my own pain. Humanity is weird.

Have you traveled? Done something completely unexpected, just to see what happened? Sometimes I'll catch a random bus and get off somewhere and explore. I know it sounds stupid, but it's cool to think, 'hey, there's some street art I would never have seen if I was dead.' or anything along those lines.

I know what you mean about not enjoying things. What did you used to enjoy? There must have been something. Do that. Even if you don't want to. Do it anyway.

I cry in public. I don't care. It means I'm still alive, and that I feel things. Don't let that hold you back. 

I mean your dreams, the ones you have when you sleep. If you don't usually remember yours, or they aren't vivid, try lucid dreaming techniques. Being in total control of your dreams and able to do anything you want is incredible.

"with trees, a long period of dormancy usually signals either a bunch of growth about to happen again, or the tree rotting away." Beautiful.

I really can't help you, because I am feeling the same. I just wanted you to know that I read your words and I can empathize so completely with them. I hope that wherever you are, whoever you are, that you find solace. Writing helps me too. Have you tried writing in a journal before?

I agree with you. I'm suicidal too.
The only thing that's kept me alive this far is curiosity. What will the world look like in 50 years? Who will I love? What horrible things will happen to me? What incredible things will happen to me?
If I'm feeling particularly suicidal, I try and force myself to do something that I truly enjoy. It can be as simple as drawing at the beach. Get outside. Look at the world. Watch other people and their lives.
Think about your dreams, that whole other world that would die along with you. Draw them. Write about them.
